description: A chord builder for Regen Modular Frames: it rescales four of that module's parameter outputs into semitone intervals and stacks them into a polyphonic chord above one incoming pitch

params.text: Sets how many notes the chord has, 2 to 5. The first note is the pitch at the note input, and each further note takes its interval from the next time-table input in turn.
Chooses how the voltage beside it is converted: both settings multiply it by 2.125, then linear subtracts 5V while linear with jump point subtracts 21.33V from anything above 10.625V

inputs.text: One of the four values to convert, taken from a parameter output of Frames, 0 to 10V
The root of the chord, one volt per octave
The gate for the chord, copied out on one channel per note
Patching anything here turns the chord into an arpeggio: each rising edge steps to the next note, the pitch and gate outputs drop to one channel, and a gate of 0V restarts from the root

outputs.text: The converted voltage from the input beside it
The chord, one polyphonic channel per note, root first; while a clock is patched it is the arpeggio on a single channel instead
The gate input on one channel per note of the chord, with 0V on the channel of any note whose time-table input reads 0V; while a clock is patched it is the gate input on a single channel instead

notes: a time-table input reading exactly 0V does not add a note: that voice holds the pitch it last had and its channel of the gate output is taken to 0V.
the multiplier of 2.125 turns a full 0 to 10V sweep into 21.25V, one semitone for each step of a 256-step source, and the jump point folds the top half of that sweep to negative semitones.
each converted output is only written while it is patched, and the chord and gate outputs only while they are patched.
